audits.title: Getting it right first time (GIRFT): A closed loop study of hip arthroplasty documentation in a trauma and orthopaedic department.
audits.standard: GIRFT, British Hip Society and BOA July 2019 total hip arthroplasty best practice guidance (24 documentation criteria)
audits.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic Department, University Hospital of North Tees; elective hip arthroplasty operative notes

cycle1.result: Handwritten notes scored an average of 12/24 (50%); compliance ranged 0%-100% across criteria, e.g. protection of critical structures 15%, leg length/neurovascular status 20%, intraoperative complications 5%; 80% legible

audits.intervention: Pre-populated GIRFT-compliant online hip arthroplasty operative note proforma in the local 'Trackcare' electronic system, typed notes

cycle2.result: Typed notes with the computerised proforma scored an average of 22/24 (92%) (p<0.05); compliance 80%-100% across criteria; 15 of 24 criteria significantly improved; 100% legible

audits.other_findings: 25 handwritten notes were collected in cycle 1 and 5 illegible notes excluded. Anaesthetist name and grade stayed at 80%; average documentation time fell from 25 to 7 minutes.
audits.citation: Sandhu J, Sharma H, Jabr Y, Sidaginamale R, Logishetty R, Cooke N, et al.. Getting it right first time (GIRFT): A closed loop study of hip arthroplasty documentation in a trauma and orthopaedic department. Ann Med Surg (Lond). 2021;61:110-114. doi:10.1016/j.amsu.2020.12.032. PMID: 33437472.

audits.title: Improving the Quality of Medical Documentation in Orthopedic Surgical Notes Using the Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR) Score.
audits.standard: Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR), based on Royal College of Surgeons guidance on medical record keeping (no target stated)
audits.setting: Jordan University Hospital, Amman, tertiary academic hospital; elective orthopaedic surgery records
audits.intervention: Annual teaching of practitioners on documentation using slides based on Royal College of Surgeons of England recommendations, with periodic (annual) re-auditing.
audits.other_findings: Yearly audits 2016–2021 (454 records) showed scores of 95.5, 95.9, 95.7 and 96.8 for 2017–2020; consent and anaesthetic domains plateaued. Benefits on the consent form and post-op instructions were never documented, and suture details fell to 41.5%.
audits.citation: Mafrachi B, Al-Ani A, Al Debei A, Elfawair M, Al-Somadi H, Shahin M, et al.. Improving the Quality of Medical Documentation in Orthopedic Surgical Notes Using the Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR) Score. Cureus. 2021;13(11):e19193. doi:10.7759/cureus.19193. PMID: 34873533.

audits.title: Assessing the Quality of Operative Notes in the Orthopedic Surgery Department at Gezira Traumatology Center, Sudan, in Accordance With the Royal College of Surgeons Guidelines.
audits.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice operative note guidance (14 parameters)
audits.setting: Orthopaedic Surgery Department, Gezira Traumatology Center, Wad Madani Teaching Hospital

cycle1.result: Mean compliance 82.0%; theatre anaesthetist name 1 (4.3%), anticipated blood loss 3 (13%), antibiotic prophylaxis 2 (8.7%), complications 12 (52.2%); procedure 22 (95.7%) and signature 23 (100%)

audits.intervention: Staff education, a standardised RCS-aligned operative note template, posters in theatres and staff areas, and a senior feedback mechanism

cycle2.result: Mean compliance 83.4%; anaesthetist name 19 (82.6%), anticipated blood loss 19 (82.6%), antibiotic prophylaxis 16 (69.6%), complications 21 (91.3%)

audits.other_findings: Prosthesis identification fell from 20 (87%) to 6 (26.1%) and tissue details from 20 (87%) to 15 (65.2%); incision and closure documentation also declined.

audits.title: Improving the Completeness of Orthopaedic Operation Notes Through a Two-Cycle Clinical Audit at Prince Osman Digna Referral Hospital.
audits.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice: 18 core operation note criteria
audits.setting: Orthopaedic department, Prince Osman Digna Referral Hospital, Port Sudan (tertiary referral centre), handwritten notes

cycle1.period: not reported (audit ran May 2024 to May 2025)
cycle1.result: Anticipated blood loss, antibiotic prophylaxis and DVT prophylaxis each 0/50 (0%); operative findings 17/50 (34%); tissue removed/altered 16/50 (32%); surgical approach 20/50 (40%); surgeon name 49/50 (98%).

audits.intervention: Presentation of findings at a governance meeting, distribution and discussion of RCS operation note standards, and senior-led feedback and reinforcement in theatre.

cycle2.result: Anticipated blood loss 10/35 (28.6%); antibiotic prophylaxis 7/35 (20%); DVT prophylaxis 5/35 (14.3%); operative findings 26/35 (74.3%); tissue altered 25/35 (71.4%); surgical approach 28/35 (80%); surgeon name 35/35 (100%).

audits.other_findings: Elective/emergency status stayed poor at 11/35 (31.4%) and surgeon signature was 30/35 (85.7%). The authors recommend a mandatory operation note template.
audits.citation: Hassan Ibrahim K, Eljack H, Elbahi MK, Mohammed Hamed FJ, Mahmoud M, Salih RAMO, et al.. Improving the Completeness of Orthopaedic Operation Notes Through a Two-Cycle Clinical Audit at Prince Osman Digna Referral Hospital. Cureus. 2026;18(1):e102633. doi:10.7759/cureus.102633. PMID: 41773159.
